title: OSINT basics
practice: Capture a mock page and rule out a false match.

lessons.title: Public and private information
lessons.intro: Open source research uses public information. Private material needs specific authority, and using a false identity to get it is deception. Check what your intake form allows.

tryit.prompt: Can you view it with public access only?

check.q: A profile is private. With public access only you…
options: Use a fake account to follow it
Leave it and ask for authority if it is necessary

check.q: Where do you check what you may access?
Collecting about people with no link to the case is…

lessons.title: Capturing a page properly
lessons.intro: Pages change and disappear. A proper capture records the address, the time and a hash, so you can show what you saw. A quick screenshot records none of that.

tryit.prompt: Which capture can you rely on in a report?
options: No address, time or hash. It cannot show what was on the page.
A full capture with address, time and hash
Right. It can be checked later.
Memory of what the page said
Memory is not evidence of what the page showed.

sandbox.task: Search the web browser for 'Linnet Close parcel' and capture the post properly.

options: The address, time and a hash
Weaker: no capture time, address or hash
check.hint: It is one of the traps.

check.q: You view a page but do not capture it, then rely on it. The problem?
options: You cannot show what it said

lessons.title: Usernames and false matches
lessons.intro: The same name or handle can belong to different people or businesses. Before you rely on a match, check other details: location, dates, what they do.

tryit.prompt: You search 'Pebble and Pine' and find a garden designer in Saltmarsh, founded 2011. The shop you are looking at sells clocks online from Kestrel Bay.
options: Different town, different trade. It is a false match.
It is a different business with a similar name
Right. Always rule out false matches.
It proves the shop is fake
A similar name proves nothing about the shop.

sandbox.task: Open the Saltmarsh business page (PG-002) in the web browser.

check.q: Two accounts share a handle. You should…
options: Assume they are the same person
Compare other details before linking them
check.hint: Handles are not unique across sites.

check.q: Which detail helps rule out a false match?
Linking the wrong account to someone is…
options: A serious mistake that can mislead the whole enquiry

lessons.title: Image clues and metadata
lessons.intro: Images hold clues: signs, door numbers, landmarks and sometimes metadata such as the time taken or a location. Many platforms strip metadata, so check what is really there.

tryit.prompt: Reveal the metadata of the shop's label photo.
fields: The shop photographs every label before collection.
tryit.after: The photo was taken one minute after packing, which supports the packing log.

sandbox.task: Examine the label photo (EV-004) and look at its metadata.

check.q: A photo on a social platform has no metadata. Why?
options: Many platforms strip it on upload

check.q: A visible door number in a photo is…
Metadata says when a photo was taken. You should…
check.hint: Device clocks can be wrong too.
